name: ferry-building-kit
summary: I rebuilt the bay side (south face, plus the east-end lunettes) in a new pass, parts/bayside.mjs, which runs after all the other parts in build.mjs. Each module now has big round-arched fan lights (white frame, dark mullions spreading from the centre, keystone) over a gallery of arches with lit shopfronts behind, and a white cornice line between the storeys. Plot 0 has the greatest fan light in its gable over a dark MARKETPLACE band; plot 2 has fan lights in its gables and east end, with striped awnings, market tents and café umbrellas on a covered terrace. A diff against v2 shows nothing changed outside the bay side and the x 100 lunettes. The check finds no floating or orphan blocks, every indoor floor cell is lit, the plot 1 bay side is still an exact mirror about x 55.5 (so it tiles), and build.nbt is saved.

revisions.comment:
Owner's fix round for the Ferry Building kit (v1 -> v2). Keep everything that works: the white tower over the long arcade,
the grey nave with its glazed skylight, the plots and their stated sizes. Fix:
1. CLOCK FACES. The tower shaft has only narrow slits where the clocks belong. Put a big round clock face on each of its four
   sides near the top of the shaft (about y 58..68, about 11 across): a white dial (white concrete / quartz / calcite) in a
   dark round frame, twelve dark hour marks, dark hands showing about 10 past 10, glowstone or sea lantern behind so it reads
   lit. Round, not square: step the edge so it reads as a circle from the front.
2. NAVE ROOF. Part of the nave roof was never built: the nave is open to the sky in places (the unfinished parts). Close it so
   every module is roofed over its whole depth: the grey roof slopes up from both long walls to the glazed skylight ridge,
   continuous along x, and the wing section (plot 1) still TILES seamlessly end to end.
3. THE ODD GABLE. One gable is a dark, steep, spiky roof unlike the rest. Make the bay-side halls one family: grey walls and
   roofs (andesite / stone / deepslate tiles), gables with the huge round-arched lunette windows from the photo of the south end.
Also check: every module stays inside its plot (nothing past its x or z range, nothing above its height), the land front faces
north in every module, and no mob can spawn inside (light the nave and arcade).
revisions.summary: Clock faces now built on all four tower sides (round 11-wide dials, closed dark frame, 12 hour marks, 10:10 hands, glowstone behind). Nave roof slopes rebuilt cell by cell over every plot to the glazed skylight (seam x48 matches x64, plot 1 still tiles). Bay-side halls made one grey family: all gables lowered to the nave's half-block-per-cell pitch, stone-brick grey roofs (plot 2 hall + both cross-gables finally roofed), lunettes glazed. Nave, arcades, galleries and halls lit with no dark floor left.
applied: 1 CLOCK FACES: v1's clock-lights part was refused wholesale (clockFace is all-or-nothing and the shaft wall behind each dial was already solid). The tower part now lays clockFace (r4, centre y63, N z0 / S z16 / W x15 / E x31) before its walls, so the 3x3 glowstone sits in the wall. It then closes the library's white bezel notches at 12/3/6/9 and adds twelve black_concrete hour marks at radius 4. Verified in a zoom render: round, ringed, marked, hands at 10:10.

2 NAVE ROOF: naveRoofProfile refused its whole box over the tower keep, so no slope was built anywhere. roofs.mjs now builds every pitched roof as one height field written cell by cell into air: deepslate_tile stairs and top slabs rising from y27 at both long walls to the existing glass monitor, x0..99 on all plots. Plot 1 seam: roof cells at x48 match x64 (0 diffs).

3 ODD GABLE: retired roof.json (the steep deepslate roof with a quartz verge) to roof.v1.json. Every bay-side gable (plot 0 hall, plot 2 cross-gables, plot 2 east bay gable) now uses the nave's 1-in-2 pitch with grey stone_brick stairs, slabs and ridge, and grey polished_andesite gable walls cut to the roof line. Plot 2's hall and cross-gables, previously bare wall triangles with no roof, are now roofed and meet in valleys. Added closing gable walls at plot 0's z58 and plot 2's x64, and glazed the great lunettes (gray panes, polished_deepslate centre mullion and transom).

CHECKS: max y per plot is 103 / 38 / 38 (limits 104 / 38 / 42); everything is inside x0..101 and z0..79; the land front still faces north. Light: the naves of all plots, the outer arcade walks, the corner walk, both galleries and plot 0's bay hall are now lit to light ≥1 everywhere (no spawn cells). This uses stone_brick_wall lamp posts with lanterns, low hung lanterns in the walks, gallery lanterns, and lanterns on the deck under plot 2's new hall roof. mcd check: 0 floating blocks, 0 orphans. Rendered and inspected all four sides.
skipped: Palette light-on-light trim warnings (quartz trim on calcite / smooth quartz): already there in v1 and not part of the comment.
mcd fit 'hallway to nowhere' in plot 2's bay hall: comes from that room's furniture layout, already there in v1, not asked for.
Plot 1 was left exactly as in v1 apart from its roof: its nave and arcade were already fully lit.

revisions.comment:
Owner: "The bay side of the build is really plain." Revise the BAY SIDE (the south face, high z, of every module) only; keep
the land front, tower, roofs and nave exactly as in v2, the plots and sizes, and the wing section's seamless tiling along x.
Reference photos of the real bay side: /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/ferry-building/04-south-end.jpg (the south end's grey gables over the market terrace) and
/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/ferry-building/05-bay-side.jpg (the long bay facade from the water); also /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/ferry-building/06-high-roof-plan.jpg. Look at them.
1. WING SECTION (plot 1) bay face: one big round-arched FAN-LIGHT window per section in the upper storey, nearly the
   section's width, with radiating mullions (dark iron bars / dark glass panes on a light frame) and a keystone; under it a
   lower storey of arched openings (a gallery along the water) with lit shopfronts behind; a white cornice line between the
   storeys and a cornice with a modest parapet at the top. The rhythm of big fan lights repeating along the whole bay side
   is the point. It must still tile seamlessly end to end.
2. TOWER MODULE (plot 0) bay face: a tall central gable with the greatest fan light, pilasters each side, and a sign band
   under it (a long dark band with light lettering blocks suggesting "MARKETPLACE"; blocks, not entities).
3. END PAVILION (plot 2) bay face and east end: as in the south-end photo: a run of grey gables, each with a huge fan-light
   lunette, a lower block between them; along the ground a row of canvas awnings (striped or tan: banner-like wool / carpet
   on fence posts or trapdoors), and on the terrace in front, inside the plot, a few market tents (white and blue wool
   canopies on fence posts) and café tables with umbrellas.
Colour: light and mid grey walls (light gray concrete, stone, andesite), white trim (calcite, quartz), dark window frames.
Light everything so no mob spawns. Nothing may leave its plot; the land front faces north in every module as before.

applied: Plot 1 upper storey: one round-arched fan light per section, 12 wide (x 50..61, y 14..24). It has a calcite frame and sill, polished_deepslate mullions (vertical bars, a transom at the spring line, a small inner arch and rays at 45 and 90 degrees), light-grey panes so the dark bars show up, and a quartz_bricks keystone at y 25. The centre pilaster now stops at the string course instead of running across the window.

Plot 1 lower storey: a gallery along the water. Two 6-wide round arches at z 78 with calcite surrounds and keystones open onto a 4-deep walk (z 74..77) with a ceiling at y 11. Behind it, at z 73, are glazed shopfronts with dark oak door pairs and a dark band at y 8, lit by lanterns on barrel stands behind the glass. Lanterns hang on chains in the gallery, placed in mirror pairs so the section still tiles; I checked that the plot 1 bay side is an exact mirror.

White line between the storeys (smooth_quartz at y 11 in the wall, smooth_quartz_slab sill at z 79). The existing white cornice (smooth_quartz + quartz_stairs) and andesite_wall parapet stay as they were.

Plot 0: the side bars (x 0..12 and 34..47) got the same gallery and an 8-wide fan light each, mirrored about x 23. The central gable has the greatest fan light (13 wide, y 14..28, keystone y 29) with white calcite pilasters on both sides. Under it is a dark polished_deepslate sign band (y 8..10) with 11 light blocks for MARKETPLACE, and below that a glazed entrance with a dark oak door pair and a half-slab step.

Plot 2: both cross-gables now have 9-wide fan lights with keystones; the lower blocks between them get small arched windows. The two east-end lunettes on x 100 (nave end and bay hall end) were redone as framed fan lights. Along the whole ground floor (x 65..99) there is a gallery terrace: arches at z 78, shopfronts at z 73, and red-and-white striped wool awnings on spruce fence posts.

Plot 2 terrace furniture: two market tents (white and blue wool canopies on fence posts, with a barrel-and-slab counter) and three café tables with umbrellas (fence pole, blue and white wool canopy, stair chairs).

Lighting: no floor cell indoors or in the galleries is at light level 0 (`mcd light`). The structure check shows 0 floating blocks, 0 unsupported attachments and 0 orphans. Nothing is written outside x 0..101 / z 0..79.
skipped: The plot 2 terrace has no open ground in front of it: the bay face is at z 78 and the plot ends at z 79, so only one cell is left. I did the nearest sensible thing: I pulled the ground-floor shopfronts back to z 73 and put the tents and café tables on the 4-deep covered gallery terrace behind the arches. They are under cover, not in the open as in the photo.
MARKETPLACE is not legible: an 11-letter word won't fit as block letters in a 17-wide band at this scale. It is 11 alternating light quartz blocks on the dark band, suggesting a line of lettering.
Wall colour stays polished_andesite (mid grey); I didn't switch to light gray concrete. White trim is calcite and quartz, as asked.
v2's single service door at x 51..52 in plot 1 is gone: the new gallery shopfronts replace it, and removing it makes the section exactly symmetric.

Two things were already true in v2 and are unchanged: the clock room is unreachable on the walk check, and the plot 2 bay hall is partly blocked. Both are outside this comment. A few of v2's standing lanterns in the plot 2 hall near z 74..76 were removed because the terrace now occupies that space.
